title: Your Agentic Workflow's Cache Keepalive Costs 8x Too Much (v2: the interval frontier)
excerpt: Updated with the full retention curve and the interval frontier: the keepalive saves on Anthropic AND OpenAI inside each provider's paying band, OpenAI's optimal interval is 8 minutes not 4, and an interval past the TTL is actively toxic: every ping re-prefills a dead cache at full price.
content_html:
Updated with the full retention curve and the interval frontier: the keepalive saves on Anthropic AND OpenAI inside each provider's paying band, OpenAI's optimal interval is 8 minutes not 4, and an interval past the TTL is actively toxic: every ping re-prefills a dead cache at full price.

A cache keepalive is the one optimization every agent builder agrees on, and almost everyone runs it at the wrong setting.

The convention is to ping every 30 seconds. That convention costs 8× more than necessary.

I measured keepalive economics across Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and DeepSeek, with a harness that can prove its own timing. The numbers rearranged a few of my beliefs. The right interval is about 4 minutes, not 30 seconds.

Does the keepalive save you money? That depends on the provider and on how long your agent pauses. The rule: keep the cache warm only when your pause is longer than the provider's eviction point but shorter than its break-even horizon. Inside that window the keepalive pays. On Anthropic and OpenAI it saves real money. On DeepSeek and Gemini it buys only latency. Outside the window it's pure waste.

The pause that eats the cache

Provider prompt caches are one of the best deals in the API: send a prefix the server processed a moment ago, and you pay about a tenth of the input price and skip most of the prefill latency. But the cache expires in minutes, and agentic workloads are the worst possible user of it.

An agent thinks, acts, waits. It fires a request, runs a build or a test suite or sits on a human approval for ten minutes, and only then sends the follow-up that would have reused the (now large) conversation prefix. The pause outlives the cache. The follow-up pays full price and full latency. At agent scale, that's a real line item.

The defense is well known. Re-send the exact prefix on a timer during the pause; every read refreshes the TTL. Aider shipped it in 2024, Anthropic's docs recommend it, and community posts worked out the Anthropic cost mechanics and even a 4-minute interval on paper. The folklore, it turns out, had part of the right answer. What it didn't have was measurement.

Everything above is practice and arithmetic. Everything below is measured: four providers, idle gaps out to forty minutes, ping intervals out to fifteen, three independent runs, every call timestamped.

Credit where the project started: in a conference room in Bellevue, at AgentSys, where I saw Haiying Shen and Simon Peter present CacheWise, their study of KV-cache management for coding agents. Their trace analysis shows from the serving side exactly the problem above: agent sessions reuse enormous prefixes, and naive eviction wrecks them. Their question was how the server should manage the cache for agents; mine became what the client can do about it on its own. The keepalive is the client's answer, and this study is my thanks for the inspiration.

Where each cache actually dies

To know whether a keepalive is worth it, you first have to know when the cache would have died on its own. So I let idle prefixes sit, with no keepalive, and measured the warm rate out to forty minutes.

Two things fall out of this curve, and both matter.

First: the documented TTL is exactly what you can rely on, and no more. Nothing evicted before its documented TTL, and nothing past it is guaranteed. Anthropic's cache falls off a cliff between 5 and 6 minutes, exactly at its advertised 5-minute TTL. No grace period. DeepSeek is gone by 10. OpenAI actually outlives its documented 5 to 10 minutes, still half warm at 20, before going fully cold by 30. A pleasant bonus, but not one you can plan around. Google never converges at all, hovering at a 33 to 83 percent hit rate at every gap. That's not a retention curve. That's a routing lottery.

So the retention window you can assume by default is the shortest documented TTL in your fleet, minus a margin. Warmth below it held everywhere I measured. Warmth above it is luck.

Second, and this corrected my own earlier conclusion: OpenAI is not sticky, it is slow. When I first measured only to ten minutes, OpenAI looked like it never evicted. It does. I just had not waited long enough. That distinction turns out to decide whether the keepalive ever pays for it.

The keepalive itself works everywhere, and that part was never in doubt. Wherever a baseline drops, the keepalive holds the same prefix warm:

The real question isn't whether the keepalive works. It's whether it's worth paying for. And that depends on where you sit on the retention curve above.

The interval is the whole game

Here is the entire economics of the keepalive, and it is settled arithmetic:

  1. A ping costs the read price (≈10% of input) every interval τ. Holding a prefix costs 0.1× per τ.
  2. A re-prefill costs 100% once (125% on Anthropic, which bills the cache write).
  3. So spend per hour falls as 1/τ, and the interval buys nothing except safety. The optimal interval is the largest one safely under the provider's retention: ≈ 4 minutes at Anthropic's 5-minute TTL. (Hold that thought; the last section shows what "safely under" is worth, and what happens when you cross it.)
  4. Break-even is idle ≈ τ(w/r − 1): about 46 minutes at Anthropic's prices, 36 for OpenAI and DeepSeek, 12 for Google (its cached reads are 0.25×, not 0.1×). Past that, stop pinging: let the cache die and pay the re-prefill.

That last one is the rule worth internalizing, so here it is as insurance. Every ping is a premium you pay to avoid one claim: the re-prefill. On Anthropic the premium is 0.1× the input price and the claim is 1.25×, so the claim is worth about twelve premiums. Pay one premium every 4 minutes and the premiums exceed the claim after roughly eleven of them: 46 minutes of pause. That's the line.

Concretely, on a 100k-token Anthropic prefix (about $0.30 of input at list price): each ping costs $0.03, and a cold re-prefill costs $0.38.

  • 10-minute pause: two pings, $0.06, and you skip the $0.38. Keep it warm. You are 6× ahead.
  • 46-minute pause: eleven pings, $0.33, versus the $0.38 re-prefill. Roughly a wash. This is the line.
  • 1-hour pause: fifteen pings, $0.45, to avoid a $0.38 re-prefill. Stop pinging. Let the cache go cold and pay the re-prefill when you come back.

The formula tells you where your own line sits once you plug in your prices and interval. The point is that there is a line. It's closer than people assume. And past it, the disciplined move is to stop paying premiums on a policy you will never claim.

The 30-second convention everyone copies has a break-even of about 6 minutes, which is why it loses money at a 10-minute gap on all four providers. I ran the 4-minute arm too: pings fired at +240.1s and +480.1s (0.1s drift), held 23 of 24 samples warm, and cost 7.8× less than the 30-second arm for the same warmth. The convention isn't cautious. It's just expensive.

Look at the last column. At a 10-minute pause, only Anthropic and DeepSeek have evicted, so only they have anything to insure. Even there, the 30-second convention loses money.

That is what I first published: at 10 minutes, only Anthropic actually saved. But that was a fact about 10 minutes, not about the providers. OpenAI and Gemini were still warm at 10 minutes, so of course keeping them warm bought nothing. The real question: what happens once they evict?

The paying band, measured

So I ran it again at a 30-minute pause, where the retention curve says every provider except Gemini is fully cold. Now there is a re-prefill to avoid on all of them. Same 4-minute keepalive, same 100k prefix:

1800s idle, 100k prefixLet it dieKeepalive 240sVerdict
Anthropic Sonnet 4.5$0.333 (cold, 2.9s TTFT)$0.214saves 1.56×
OpenAI GPT-5.1$0.104 (cold, 4.4s TTFT)$0.085saves 1.23×
DeepSeek V3.2$0.022 (cold, 5.4s TTFT)$0.108loses; buys latency

There it is. Once OpenAI actually evicts, its keepalive saves money too. The keepalive was never an Anthropic-only trick. It pays for any provider once your pause is long enough to reach eviction and short enough to stay under break-even.

Each provider has a band where this holds: Anthropic from about 5 to 46 minutes; OpenAI from about 30 minutes out to over an hour at its own best interval (next section). Outside the band, on either side, you are paying premiums for nothing.

DeepSeek is the honest exception. It does evict, but a cold re-prefill costs two cents, so the pings cost more than the eviction they prevent no matter how you time them. Its keepalive is a latency play only: 5.4 seconds to first token down to 2.0.

Gemini is worse: it never reliably evicts (its hit rate is a routing lottery, not a retention curve) and its cached reads cost 0.25× instead of 0.1×, so there is no pause length where keeping it warm pays on cost. For those two, keep warm only if you are buying speed, never dollars.

Past the TTL, pings turn toxic

One question remained. If keepalive cost falls as the interval grows, why stop at 4 minutes? So I kept going: same 30-minute pause, same prefix, ping intervals of 4, 8, and 15 minutes.

The interval is bounded by the provider's own retention, and the chart shows both sides of that line.

OpenAI's cache holds 8-minute gaps, so 8-minute pings halve its cost again: $0.042 against a $0.104 re-prefill, a 2.45× saving, double what 4-minute pings deliver. Its true optimal interval is about 8 minutes, not 4.

Anthropic at 8-minute pings is a catastrophe, and the reason matters. Its cache dies at 5 minutes, so every 8-minute ping lands on a dead cache and re-prefills it at full write price. Three pings, three full prefills, and you still arrive warm only by accident of timing. The bill: $1.334, four times the cost of never pinging at all. An interval past the TTL isn't merely wasteful. Every ping pays the exact penalty it was meant to avoid.

Nobody survives 15-minute pings, and DeepSeek at 8 minutes is a coin flip (its cache dies around 9). So the sharpened rule: the economical interval is your provider's own measured retention minus a margin, and it is per-provider. Four minutes on Anthropic. Eight on OpenAI. A multi-provider agent that uses one global ping interval is either overpaying on OpenAI or burning money on Anthropic.

What is settled, and what I believe

Settled: the arithmetic above, the measured retention curves, the measured 7.8×, the break-even horizons, and the interval frontier with its toxic edge. Those you can check against the data, which is public with the harness.

Belief: what happens when everyone takes this advice. A cache tier's eviction policy ranks by expected reuse; a keepalive manufactures recency, so once every client pings, LRU has nothing left to rank and the tier degrades for everyone. Residency today is priced per read, not per token-hour held, so each operator's rational rent payment imposes an unpriced cost on every other tenant. My prediction: keepalive adoption forces providers to meter residency directly. Google's explicit cache already bills per token-hour, and Anthropic's 1-hour tier at 2× write is a step in the same direction. The arbitrage is real, and it has an expiry date.

The policy

  • Keep warm only across bounded, plausibly reused pauses (a tool call, an approval wait), at τ* set per provider to its measured retention minus a margin. About 4 minutes on Anthropic, 8 on OpenAI, 50 on Anthropic's 1-hour tier.
  • Never let τ exceed the provider's retention. Past it, every ping re-prefills a dead cache at full price and the keepalive costs more than doing nothing (4× more, on Anthropic at 8-minute pings).
  • Abandon the keepalive past the break-even horizon (≈46 minutes at Anthropic prices). Let it die, re-prefill, walk away.
  • Stay inside the paying band. Keep warm only when your pause is longer than the provider's eviction point (Anthropic ~5 min, OpenAI ~30 min, DeepSeek ~10 min, Gemini never) and shorter than its break-even. Anthropic and OpenAI save money inside their bands. DeepSeek and Gemini never save on cost, only latency.
  • Below the eviction point, do not bother. The cache is still warm on its own, so the pings buy nothing. This is the mistake the 30-second convention makes on every provider.
  • Never keep a dead session warm. The pi agent harness implements exactly this: pings only while a tool batch runs, default off.

Keep it warm, briefly, at your provider's own rate. Ping less, but never slower than the cache forgets.

  • Aider AI. Change history (cache keepalive, v0.53.0, 2024).
  • Anthropic. Prompt caching (pre-warming guidance).
  • Veritas Supera. We Taught Our AI Agents to Take Coffee Breaks (the 4-minute interval, on paper).
  • Brandon Wie. Anthropic Prompt Cache TTL + Cost Mechanics.

  • Don't Break the Cache (what to cache for agentic tasks, a different question).

blocks.html_en: Does the keepalive save you money? That depends on the provider and on how long your agent pauses. The rule: keep the cache warm only when your pause is longer than the provider's eviction point but shorter than its break-even horizon. Inside that window the keepalive pays. On Anthropic and OpenAI it saves real money. On DeepSeek and Gemini it buys only latency. Outside the window it's pure waste.

sentences.en: The rule: keep the cache warm only when your pause is longer than the provider's eviction point but shorter than its break-even horizon.

sentences.en: Inside that window the keepalive pays.
sentences.zh: 在该窗口内，保活是有代价的。

sentences.en: On Anthropic and OpenAI it saves real money.
sentences.zh: 在 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 上它可以节省真正的钱。

sentences.en: On DeepSeek and Gemini it buys only latency.
sentences.zh: 在 DeepSeek 和 Gemini 上，它只购买延迟。

sentences.en: Outside the window it's pure waste.
sentences.zh: 窗外完全是垃圾。

sentences.en: The pause that eats the cache

blocks.html_en: Provider prompt caches are one of the best deals in the API: send a prefix the server processed a moment ago, and you pay about a tenth of the input price and skip most of the prefill latency. But the cache expires in minutes, and agentic workloads are the worst possible user of it.

sentences.en: Provider prompt caches are one of the best deals in the API: send a prefix the server processed a moment ago, and you pay about a tenth of the input price and skip most of the prefill latency.
sentences.zh: 提供者提示缓存是 API 中最好的交易之一：发送服务器刚才处理的前缀，您只需支付大约十分之一的输入价格，并跳过大部分预填充延迟。

sentences.en: But the cache expires in minutes, and agentic workloads are the worst possible user of it.
sentences.zh: 但缓存在几分钟内就会过期，而代理工作负载可能是最糟糕的用户。

blocks.html_en: An agent thinks, acts, waits. It fires a request, runs a build or a test suite or sits on a human approval for ten minutes, and only then sends the follow-up that would have reused the (now large) conversation prefix. The pause outlives the cache. The follow-up pays full price and full latency. At agent scale, that's a real line item.

blocks.html_en: The defense is well known. Re-send the exact prefix on a timer during the pause; every read refreshes the TTL. Aider shipped it in 2024, Anthropic's docs recommend it, and community posts worked out the Anthropic cost mechanics and even a 4-minute interval on paper. The folklore, it turns out, had part of the right answer. What it didn't have was measurement.

sentences.en: Aider shipped it in 2024, Anthropic's docs recommend it, and community posts worked out the Anthropic cost mechanics and even a 4-minute interval on paper.
sentences.zh: Aider 在 2024 年发布了它，Anthropic 的文档推荐了它，社区帖子制定了 Anthropic 成本机制，甚至在纸上确定了 4 分钟的间隔。

blocks.html_en: Everything above is practice and arithmetic. Everything below is measured: four providers, idle gaps out to forty minutes, ping intervals out to fifteen, three independent runs, every call timestamped.

blocks.html_en: Credit where the project started: in a conference room in Bellevue, at AgentSys, where I saw Haiying Shen and Simon Peter present CacheWise, their study of KV-cache management for coding agents. Their trace analysis shows from the serving side exactly the problem above: agent sessions reuse enormous prefixes, and naive eviction wrecks them. Their question was how the server should manage the cache for agents; mine became what the client can do about it on its own. The keepalive is the client's answer, and this study is my thanks for the inspiration.

sentences.en: Where each cache actually dies

blocks.html_en: To know whether a keepalive is worth it, you first have to know when the cache would have died on its own. So I let idle prefixes sit, with no keepalive, and measured the warm rate out to forty minutes.

sentences.en: To know whether a keepalive is worth it, you first have to know when the cache would have died on its own.
sentences.zh: 要知道保持活动是否值得，您首先必须知道缓存何时会自行失效。

sentences.en: So I let idle prefixes sit, with no keepalive, and measured the warm rate out to forty minutes.
sentences.zh: 因此，我让空闲前缀闲置，没有保活，并将温暖速率测量为四十分钟。

sentences.en: Idle cache survival with no keepalive, 100k prefix.
sentences.zh: 无 keepalive、100k 前缀的空闲缓存生存。

sentences.en: The green band is the window where every provider is still warm.
sentences.zh: 绿色带是每个提供者仍然温暖的窗口。

blocks.html_en: Two things fall out of this curve, and both matter.

sentences.en: Two things fall out of this curve, and both matter.
sentences.zh: 有两件事超出了这条曲线，而且都很重要。

blocks.html_en: First: the documented TTL is exactly what you can rely on, and no more. Nothing evicted before its documented TTL, and nothing past it is guaranteed. Anthropic's cache falls off a cliff between 5 and 6 minutes, exactly at its advertised 5-minute TTL. No grace period. DeepSeek is gone by 10. OpenAI actually outlives its documented 5 to 10 minutes, still half warm at 20, before going fully cold by 30. A pleasant bonus, but not one you can plan around. Google never converges at all, hovering at a 33 to 83 percent hit rate at every gap. That's not a retention curve. That's a routing lottery.

sentences.en: First: the documented TTL is exactly what you can rely on, and no more.
sentences.zh: 首先：记录的 TTL 正是您可以信赖的，仅此而已。

sentences.en: Nothing evicted before its documented TTL, and nothing past it is guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 在其记录的 TTL 之前不会驱逐任何内容，并且在超过该 TTL 后不会保证任何内容。

sentences.en: Anthropic's cache falls off a cliff between 5 and 6 minutes, exactly at its advertised 5-minute TTL.
sentences.zh: Anthropic 的缓存在 5 到 6 分钟内急剧下降，正好达到其宣传的 5 分钟 TTL。

sentences.en: No grace period.
sentences.zh: 没有宽限期。

sentences.en: DeepSeek is gone by 10.
sentences.zh: DeepSeek 下降了 10。

sentences.en: OpenAI actually outlives its documented 5 to 10 minutes, still half warm at 20, before going fully cold by 30.
sentences.zh: OpenAI 实际上比其记录的寿命长了 5 到 10 分钟，在 20 ℃ 时仍处于半热状态，然后在 30 ℃ 时完全变冷。

sentences.en: A pleasant bonus, but not one you can plan around.
sentences.zh: 这是一项令人愉快的奖励，但不是你可以计划的。

sentences.en: Google never converges at all, hovering at a 33 to 83 percent hit rate at every gap.
sentences.zh: Google 根本不会收敛，每次差距的命中率都徘徊在 33% 到 83% 之间。

sentences.en: That's not a retention curve.
sentences.zh: 这不是保留曲线。

sentences.en: That's a routing lottery.
sentences.zh: 这就是路由抽签。

blocks.html_en: So the retention window you can assume by default is the shortest documented TTL in your fleet, minus a margin. Warmth below it held everywhere I measured. Warmth above it is luck.

sentences.en: So the retention window you can assume by default is the shortest documented TTL in your fleet, minus a margin.
sentences.zh: 因此，默认情况下，您可以假设的保留窗口是您的队列中记录的最短 TTL 减去余量。

sentences.en: Warmth below it held everywhere I measured.
sentences.zh: 在我测量的任何地方，它下面都有温暖。

sentences.en: Warmth above it is luck.
sentences.zh: 上面有温暖就是运气。

blocks.html_en: Second, and this corrected my own earlier conclusion: OpenAI is not sticky, it is slow. When I first measured only to ten minutes, OpenAI looked like it never evicted. It does. I just had not waited long enough. That distinction turns out to decide whether the keepalive ever pays for it.

sentences.en: Second, and this corrected my own earlier conclusion: OpenAI is not sticky, it is slow.
sentences.zh: 其次，这纠正了我之前的结论：OpenAI 没有粘性，它很慢。

sentences.en: When I first measured only to ten minutes, OpenAI looked like it never evicted.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次只测量十分钟时，OpenAI 看起来好像从未被驱逐过。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I just had not waited long enough.
sentences.zh: 我只是等得不够久。

sentences.en: That distinction turns out to decide whether the keepalive ever pays for it.
sentences.zh: 这种区别最终决定了保活是否会为此付出代价。

blocks.html_en: The keepalive itself works everywhere, and that part was never in doubt. Wherever a baseline drops, the keepalive holds the same prefix warm:

sentences.en: The keepalive itself works everywhere, and that part was never in doubt.
sentences.zh: 保活本身在任何地方都有效，这一点毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Wherever a baseline drops, the keepalive holds the same prefix warm:
sentences.zh: 无论基线下降，保活都会保持相同的前缀：

sentences.en: Baseline (dashed) vs keepalive (solid) warm rate, out to 30 minutes at 100k.
sentences.zh: 基线（虚线）与 keepalive（实线）温暖速率，100k 时长达 30 分钟。

sentences.en: Anthropic: 0 of 48 warm at ten minutes without the keepalive, 40 of 40 with it.
sentences.zh: 人类：48 中的 0 人在 10 分钟内没有保活，40 人中的 40 人在有保活的情况下温暖。

sentences.en: Every provider that evicts is held at 100%.
sentences.zh: 每个驱逐的提供商都被保留为 100%。

blocks.html_en: The real question isn't whether the keepalive works. It's whether it's worth paying for. And that depends on where you sit on the retention curve above.

sentences.en: The real question isn't whether the keepalive works.
sentences.zh: 真正的问题不是保活是否有效。

sentences.en: It's whether it's worth paying for.
sentences.zh: 而是看是否值得付出代价。

sentences.en: And that depends on where you sit on the retention curve above.
sentences.zh: 这取决于您在上面的保留曲线上的位置。

blocks.html_en: The interval is the whole game

sentences.en: The interval is the whole game
sentences.zh: 间歇就是整场比赛

blocks.html_en: Here is the entire economics of the keepalive, and it is settled arithmetic:

sentences.en: Here is the entire economics of the keepalive, and it is settled arithmetic:
sentences.zh: 这是保活的整个经济学，并且是经过算术计算的：

blocks.html_en: • A ping costs the read price (≈10% of input) every interval τ. Holding a prefix costs 0.1× per τ.

sentences.en: A ping costs the read price (≈10% of input) every interval τ.
sentences.zh: 每间隔 τ 一次 ping 都会花费读取价格（约输入的 10%）。

sentences.en: Holding a prefix costs 0.1× per τ.
sentences.zh: 持有一个前缀的成本为每 τ 0.1×。

blocks.html_en: • A re-prefill costs 100% once (125% on Anthropic, which bills the cache write).

sentences.en: A re-prefill costs 100% once (125% on Anthropic, which bills the cache write).
sentences.zh: 重新预填充一次费用为 100%（Anthropic 为 125%，对缓存写入进行计费）。

blocks.html_en: • So spend per hour falls as 1/τ, and the interval buys nothing except safety. The optimal interval is the largest one safely under the provider's retention: ≈ 4 minutes at Anthropic's 5-minute TTL. (Hold that thought; the last section shows what "safely under" is worth, and what happens when you cross it.)

sentences.en: So spend per hour falls as 1/τ, and the interval buys nothing except safety.
sentences.zh: 因此，每小时的支出下降为 1/τ，而间隔除了安全之外什么也买不到。

sentences.en: The optimal interval is the largest one safely under the provider's retention: ≈ 4 minutes at Anthropic's 5-minute TTL.
sentences.zh: 最佳间隔是提供者保留的最大安全间隔：在 Anthropic 的 5 分钟 TTL 下，约 4 分钟。

sentences.en: (Hold that thought; the last section shows what "safely under" is worth, and what happens when you cross it.)
sentences.zh: （保持这个想法；最后一部分展示了“安全地”的价值，以及当你跨越它时会发生什么。）

blocks.html_en: • Break-even is idle ≈ τ(w/r − 1): about 46 minutes at Anthropic's prices, 36 for OpenAI and DeepSeek, 12 for Google (its cached reads are 0.25×, not 0.1×). Past that, stop pinging: let the cache die and pay the re-prefill.

sentences.en: Break-even is idle ≈ τ(w/r − 1): about 46 minutes at Anthropic's prices, 36 for OpenAI and DeepSeek, 12 for Google (its cached reads are 0.25×, not 0.1×).
sentences.zh: 盈亏平衡空闲 ≈ τ(w/r − 1)：以 Anthropic 的价格计算大约 46 分钟，OpenAI 和 DeepSeek 为 36 分钟，Google 为 12 分钟（其缓存读取是 0.25×，而不是 0.1×）。

sentences.en: Past that, stop pinging: let the cache die and pay the re-prefill.
sentences.zh: 之后，停止 ping：让缓存失效并支付重新预填充的费用。

blocks.html_en: That last one is the rule worth internalizing, so here it is as insurance. Every ping is a premium you pay to avoid one claim: the re-prefill. On Anthropic the premium is 0.1× the input price and the claim is 1.25×, so the claim is worth about twelve premiums. Pay one premium every 4 minutes and the premiums exceed the claim after roughly eleven of them: 46 minutes of pause. That's the line.

sentences.en: That last one is the rule worth internalizing, so here it is as insurance.
sentences.zh: 最后一条是值得内化的规则，所以在这里它是作为保险。

sentences.en: Every ping is a premium you pay to avoid one claim: the re-prefill.
sentences.zh: 每一次 ping 都是您为避免一项索赔而支付的费用：重新预充。

sentences.en: On Anthropic the premium is 0.1× the input price and the claim is 1.25×, so the claim is worth about twelve premiums.
sentences.zh: 在 Anthropic 上，保费是投入价格的 0.1 倍，索赔是 1.25 倍，因此索赔价值约为 12 倍保费。

sentences.en: Pay one premium every 4 minutes and the premiums exceed the claim after roughly eleven of them: 46 minutes of pause.
sentences.zh: 每 4 分钟支付一笔保费，大约在 11 分钟（即 46 分钟的暂停）后，保费就会超出索赔额。

sentences.en: That's the line.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

blocks.html_en: Concretely, on a 100k-token Anthropic prefix (about $0.30 of input at list price): each ping costs $0.03, and a cold re-prefill costs $0.38.

sentences.en: Concretely, on a 100k-token Anthropic prefix (about $0.30 of input at list price): each ping costs $0.03, and a cold re-prefill costs $0.38.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，对于 10 万代币的 Anthropic 前缀（按标价输入约 0.30 美元）：每个 ping 成本为 0.03 美元，冷重新预填充成本为 0.38 美元。

blocks.html_en: • 10-minute pause: two pings, $0.06, and you skip the $0.38. Keep it warm. You are 6× ahead.

sentences.en: 10-minute pause: two pings, $0.06, and you skip the $0.38.
sentences.zh: 10 分钟暂停：两次 ping，0.06 美元，然后您跳过 0.38 美元。

sentences.en: Keep it warm.
sentences.zh: 保持温暖。

sentences.en: You are 6× ahead.
sentences.zh: 您领先 6 倍。

blocks.html_en: • 46-minute pause: eleven pings, $0.33, versus the $0.38 re-prefill. Roughly a wash. This is the line.

sentences.en: 46-minute pause: eleven pings, $0.33, versus the $0.38 re-prefill.
sentences.zh: 46 分钟暂停：11 次 ping，费用为 0.33 美元，而重新预填充费用为 0.38 美元。

sentences.en: Roughly a wash.
sentences.zh: 大致洗了一下。

sentences.en: This is the line.
sentences.zh: 就是这条线。

blocks.html_en: • 1-hour pause: fifteen pings, $0.45, to avoid a $0.38 re-prefill. Stop pinging. Let the cache go cold and pay the re-prefill when you come back.

sentences.en: 1-hour pause: fifteen pings, $0.45, to avoid a $0.38 re-prefill.
sentences.zh: 1 小时暂停：15 次 ping，0.45 美元，以避免 0.38 美元的重新预充。

sentences.en: Stop pinging.
sentences.zh: 停止 ping。

sentences.en: Let the cache go cold and pay the re-prefill when you come back.
sentences.zh: 让缓存变冷并在您回来时支付重新预填充的费用。

blocks.html_en: The formula tells you where your own line sits once you plug in your prices and interval. The point is that there is a line. It's closer than people assume. And past it, the disciplined move is to stop paying premiums on a policy you will never claim.

sentences.en: The formula tells you where your own line sits once you plug in your prices and interval.
sentences.zh: 一旦您输入价格和间隔，该公式就会告诉您自己的线位于何处。

sentences.en: The point is that there is a line.
sentences.zh: 重点是有一条线。

sentences.en: It's closer than people assume.

sentences.en: And past it, the disciplined move is to stop paying premiums on a policy you will never claim.
sentences.zh: 过去了，有纪律的举动是停止为您永远不会索赔的保单支付保费。

blocks.html_en: The 30-second convention everyone copies has a break-even of about 6 minutes, which is why it loses money at a 10-minute gap on all four providers. I ran the 4-minute arm too: pings fired at +240.1s and +480.1s (0.1s drift), held 23 of 24 samples warm, and cost 7.8× less than the 30-second arm for the same warmth. The convention isn't cautious. It's just expensive.

sentences.en: The convention isn't cautious.
sentences.zh: 大会并不谨慎。

sentences.en: It's just expensive.
sentences.zh: 只是很贵。

blocks.html_en: Belief: what happens when everyone takes this advice. A cache tier's eviction policy ranks by expected reuse; a keepalive manufactures recency, so once every client pings, LRU has nothing left to rank and the tier degrades for everyone. Residency today is priced per read, not per token-hour held, so each operator's rational rent payment imposes an unpriced cost on every other tenant. My prediction: keepalive adoption forces providers to meter residency directly. Google's explicit cache already bills per token-hour, and Anthropic's 1-hour tier at 2× write is a step in the same direction. The arbitrage is real, and it has an expiry date.

blocks.html_en: • Keep warm only across bounded, plausibly reused pauses (a tool call, an approval wait), at τ* set per provider to its measured retention minus a margin. About 4 minutes on Anthropic, 8 on OpenAI, 50 on Anthropic's 1-hour tier.

sentences.en: Keep warm only across bounded, plausibly reused pauses (a tool call, an approval wait), at τ* set per provider to its measured retention minus a margin.

sentences.zh: 在 Anthropic 上大约 4 分钟，在 OpenAI 上大约 8 分钟，在 Anthropic 的 1 小时级别上大约 50 分钟。

blocks.html_en: • Never let τ exceed the provider's retention. Past it, every ping re-prefills a dead cache at full price and the keepalive costs more than doing nothing (4× more, on Anthropic at 8-minute pings).

sentences.en: Never let τ exceed the provider's retention.
sentences.zh: 切勿让 τ 超过提供商的保留量。

sentences.en: Past it, every ping re-prefills a dead cache at full price and the keepalive costs more than doing nothing (4× more, on Anthropic at 8-minute pings).
sentences.zh: 过了这个时间，每个 ping 都会以全价重新预填充死缓存，而保活的成本比什么都不做要高（在 Anthropic 上，8 分钟 ping 的成本是 4 倍）。

blocks.html_en: • Abandon the keepalive past the break-even horizon (≈46 minutes at Anthropic prices). Let it die, re-prefill, walk away.

sentences.zh: 让它消亡，重新填充，走开。

Keep warm only when your pause is longer than the provider's eviction point (Anthropic ~5 min, OpenAI ~30 min, DeepSeek ~10 min, Gemini never) and shorter than its break-even. Anthropic and OpenAI save money inside their bands. DeepSeek and Gemini never save on cost, only latency.

sentences.zh: DeepSeek 和 Gemini 从不节省成本，只节省延迟。

content_html_zh:
使用完整的保留曲线和间隔边界进行更新：Keepalive 在每个提供商的付费范围内节省了 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的费用，OpenAI 的最佳间隔是 8 分钟而不是 4 分钟，超过 TTL 的间隔是有毒的：每个 ping 都会以全价重新预填充死缓存。

缓存保活是每个代理构建者都同意的一项优化，但几乎每个人都在错误的设置下运行它。

约定是每 30 秒 ping 一次。 该会议的成本比所需成本高出 8 倍。

我使用可以证明其自身时机的工具测量了 Anthropic、OpenAI、Gemini 和 DeepSeek 的保活经济学。 这些数字重新排列了我的一些信念。 正确的间隔时间约为 4 分钟，而不是 30 秒。

keepalive 能帮你省钱吗？ 这取决于提供商以及您的代理暂停的时间。 规则：仅当您的暂停时间长于提供者的逐出点但短于其收支平衡范围时，才使缓存保持温暖。 在该窗口内，保活是有代价的。 在 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 上它可以节省真正的钱。 在 DeepSeek 和 Gemini 上，它只购买延迟。 窗外完全是垃圾。

消耗缓存的暂停

提供者提示缓存是 API 中最好的交易之一：发送服务器刚才处理的前缀，您只需支付大约十分之一的输入价格，并跳过大部分预填充延迟。 但缓存在几分钟内就会过期，而代理工作负载可能是最糟糕的用户。

代理人思考、行动、等待。 它会发出请求，运行构建或测试套件，或者等待人工批准十分钟，然后才发送将重用（现在很大）对话前缀的后续内容。 暂停的寿命比缓存的寿命长。 后续支付全价和全延迟。 在代理规模上，这是一个真正的订单项。

防守是众所周知的。 在暂停期间重新发送计时器上的确切前缀；每次读取都会刷新 TTL。 Aider 在 2024 年发布了它，Anthropic 的文档推荐了它，社区帖子制定了 Anthropic 成本机制，甚至在纸上确定了 4 分钟的间隔。 事实证明，民间传说有部分正确答案。 它没有测量。

以上一切都是练习和算术。 以下所有内容均经过测量：四个提供商、空闲间隙长达 40 分钟、ping 间隔长达 15 分钟、三次独立运行、每次调用都带有时间戳。

项目开始的地方：在贝尔维尤的 AgentSys 会议室，我看到 Haiying Shen 和 Simon Peter 展示了 CacheWise，这是他们对编码代理的 KV 缓存管理的研究。 他们的跟踪分析从服务端准确地显示了上述问题：代理会话重复使用大量前缀，而天真的驱逐会破坏它们。 他们的问题是服务器应该如何管理代理的缓存；我的变成了客户可以自己做的事情。 keepalive是客户的答案，这个研究是我感谢的启发。

每个缓存实际上失效的地方

要知道保持活动是否值得，您首先必须知道缓存何时会自行失效。 因此，我让空闲前缀闲置，没有保活，并将温暖速率测量为四十分钟。

有两件事超出了这条曲线，而且都很重要。

首先：记录的 TTL 正是您可以信赖的，仅此而已。 在其记录的 TTL 之前不会驱逐任何内容，并且在超过该 TTL 后不会保证任何内容。 Anthropic 的缓存在 5 到 6 分钟内急剧下降，正好达到其宣传的 5 分钟 TTL。 没有宽限期。 DeepSeek 下降了 10。 OpenAI 实际上比其记录的寿命长了 5 到 10 分钟，在 20 ℃ 时仍处于半热状态，然后在 30 ℃ 时完全变冷。 这是一项令人愉快的奖励，但不是你可以计划的。 Google 根本不会收敛，每次差距的命中率都徘徊在 33% 到 83% 之间。 这不是保留曲线。 这就是路由抽签。

因此，默认情况下，您可以假设的保留窗口是您的队列中记录的最短 TTL 减去余量。 在我测量的任何地方，它下面都有温暖。 上面有温暖就是运气。

其次，这纠正了我之前的结论：OpenAI 没有粘性，它很慢。 当我第一次只测量十分钟时，OpenAI 看起来好像从未被驱逐过。 确实如此。 我只是等得不够久。 这种区别最终决定了保活是否会为此付出代价。

保活本身在任何地方都有效，这一点毫无疑问。 无论基线下降，保活都会保持相同的前缀：

真正的问题不是保活是否有效。 而是看是否值得付出代价。 这取决于您在上面的保留曲线上的位置。

间歇就是整场比赛

这是保活的整个经济学，并且是经过算术计算的：

  1. 每间隔 τ 一次 ping 都会花费读取价格（约输入的 10%）。 持有一个前缀的成本为每 τ 0.1×。
  2. 重新预填充一次费用为 100%（Anthropic 为 125%，对缓存写入进行计费）。
  3. 因此，每小时的支出下降为 1/τ，而间隔除了安全之外什么也买不到。 最佳间隔是提供者保留的最大安全间隔：在 Anthropic 的 5 分钟 TTL 下，约 4 分钟。 （保持这个想法；最后一部分展示了“安全地”的价值，以及当你跨越它时会发生什么。）
  4. 盈亏平衡空闲 ≈ τ(w/r − 1)：以 Anthropic 的价格计算大约 46 分钟，OpenAI 和 DeepSeek 为 36 分钟，Google 为 12 分钟（其缓存读取是 0.25×，而不是 0.1×）。 之后，停止 ping：让缓存失效并支付重新预填充的费用。

最后一条是值得内化的规则，所以在这里它是作为保险。 每一次 ping 都是您为避免一项索赔而支付的费用：重新预充。 在 Anthropic 上，保费是投入价格的 0.1 倍，索赔是 1.25 倍，因此索赔价值约为 12 倍保费。 每 4 分钟支付一笔保费，大约在 11 分钟（即 46 分钟的暂停）后，保费就会超出索赔额。 就是这样。

具体来说，对于 10 万代币的 Anthropic 前缀（按标价输入约 0.30 美元）：每个 ping 成本为 0.03 美元，冷重新预填充成本为 0.38 美元。

  • 10 分钟暂停：两次 ping，0.06 美元，然后您跳过 0.38 美元。 保持温暖。 您领先 6 倍。
  • 46 分钟暂停：11 次 ping，费用为 0.33 美元，而重新预填充费用为 0.38 美元。 大致洗了一下。 就是这条线。
  • 1 小时暂停：15 次 ping，0.45 美元，以避免 0.38 美元的重新预充。 停止 ping。 让缓存变冷并在您回来时支付重新预填充的费用。

一旦您输入价格和间隔，该公式就会告诉您自己的线位于何处。 重点是有一条线。 它比人们想象的更接近。 过去了，有纪律的举动是停止为您永远不会索赔的保单支付保费。

每个人都复制的 30 秒惯例的盈亏平衡点约为 6 分钟，这就是为什么它在所有四个提供商的 10 分钟差距时都亏损的原因。 我也运行了 4 分钟臂：ping 发射时间为 +240.1 秒和 +480.1 秒（0.1 秒漂移），对 24 个样本中的 23 个进行了保温，并且在相同的温度下，成本比 30 秒臂少 7.8 倍。 大会并不谨慎。 只是很贵。

看最后一栏。 在 10 分钟的暂停中，只有 Anthropic 和 DeepSeek 进行了驱逐，因此只有他们有任何需要确保的东西。 即使如此，30 秒的会议也会亏损。

这就是我第一次发表的内容：10 分钟时，只有 Anthropic 真正得救了。 但这是大约 10 分钟的事实，与提供商无关。 OpenAI 和 Gemini 在 10 分钟时仍然很热，所以当然让它们保持温暖并没有什么意义。 真正的问题是：一旦他们驱逐，会发生什么？

付费范围，测量

因此，我在 30 分钟的暂停后再次运行它，保留曲线显示除 Gemini 之外的每个提供商都处于完全冷状态。 现在，所有这些都需要避免重新预填充。 相同的 4 分钟保活，相同的 100k 前缀：

1800s 空闲，100k 前缀让它死吧保持连接 240 秒判决
人择十四行诗 4.50.333 美元（冷，2.9s TTFT）$0.214saves 1.56×
OpenAI GPT-5.10.104 美元（冷，4.4s TTFT）$0.085saves 1.23×
深寻V3.2$0.022（冷，5.4s TTFT）$0.108失去；购买延迟

就在那里。 一旦 OpenAI 真正驱逐，它的 keepalive 也能省钱。 保活从来都不是人类独有的技巧。 一旦您的暂停时间足够长以实现驱逐，并且时间足够短以保持收支平衡，那么任何提供商都会付出代价。

每个提供者都有一个频段，其中： 人为的，大约 5 到 46 分钟； OpenAI 的最佳时间间隔从大约 30 分钟延长到一个多小时（下一节）。 在范围之外，无论是哪一方，您都无需支付任何费用。

DeepSeek 是一个诚实的例外。 它确实会驱逐，但冷重新预填充要花费两美分，所以无论你如何计时，ping 的成本都比它们阻止的驱逐要高。 它的 keepalive 只是一个延迟播放：第一个令牌下降到 2.0 需要 5.4 秒。

Gemini 更糟糕：它永远不会可靠地驱逐（它的命中率是路由抽签，而不是保留曲线）并且其缓存读取成本为 0.25× 而不是 0.1×，因此不存在暂停长度，保持其温暖会付出成本。 对于这两者，只有当你购买的是速度而不是金钱时才要保持温暖。

超过 TTL，ping 会变得有毒

还剩下一个问题。 如果保活成本随着间隔的增加而下降，为什么要停在 4 分钟呢？ 所以我继续：同样的 30 分钟暂停、同样的前缀、4 分钟、8 分钟和 15 分钟的 ping 间隔。

该区间以提供商自身的保留率为界限，图表显示了该线的两侧。

OpenAI 的缓存可容纳 8 分钟的间隙，因此 8 分钟 ping 的成本再次降低了一半：重新预填充 0.104 美元，成本为 0.042 美元，节省了 2.45 倍，是 4 分钟 ping 的两倍。 其真正的最佳间隔约为 8 分钟，而不是 4 分钟。

人为的 8 分钟 ping 值是一场灾难，原因很重要。 它的缓存会在 5 分钟内失效，因此每 8 分钟 ping 都会到达一个失效的缓存，并以完全写入的价格重新预填充它。 三声“ping”，三次完整的预填充，您仍然会温暖地到达，只是时间上的偶然。 费用为 1.334 美元，是根本不 ping 的成本的四倍。 超过 TTL 的时间间隔不仅仅是浪费。 每一次 ping 都会付出它本来应该避免的确切惩罚。

没有人能在 15 分钟的 ping 中幸存，而 DeepSeek 在 8 分钟时就像一枚硬币翻转（它的缓存在 9 分钟左右就失效了）。 因此，更明确的规则是：经济间隔是提供商自己测量的留存率减去利润，并且是针对每个提供商的。 《人择》上的四分钟。 OpenAI 上有八个。 使用一个全局 ping 间隔的多提供商代理要么在 OpenAI 上付出过高的代价，要么在 Anthropic 上烧钱。

已定的事和我所相信的事

已解决：上述算术、测量的保留曲线、测量的 7.8×、盈亏平衡范围以及带有毒性边缘的区间边界。 您可以根据数据进行检查，这些数据是通过线束公开的。

信念：当每个人都接受这个建议时会发生什么。 缓存层的逐出策略按预期重用进行排名； keepalive 会产生新近度，因此一旦每个客户端执行 ping 操作，LRU 就没有剩余的内容可以排名，并且每个人的级别都会降级。 如今的居住权是按每次阅读定价，而不是按持有的象征性小时定价，因此每个运营商合理的租金支付都会给其他租户带来未定价的成本。 我的预测：保活的采用迫使提供商直接计量居住情况。 Google 的显式缓存已经按令牌小时计费，而 Anthropic 的 2 次写入的 1 小时层级也是朝同一方向迈出的一步。 套利是真实的，并且有到期日。

政策

  • 仅在有界的、合理重用的暂停（工具调用、批准等待）期间保持温暖，每个提供商的 τ* 设置为其测量的留存率减去余量。 在 Anthropic 上大约 4 分钟，在 OpenAI 上大约 8 分钟，在 Anthropic 的 1 小时级别上大约 50 分钟。
  • 切勿让 τ 超过提供商的保留量。 过了这个时间，每个 ping 都会以全价重新预填充死缓存，而保活的成本比什么都不做要高（在 Anthropic 上，8 分钟 ping 的成本是 4 倍）。
  • 超过收支平衡范围后放弃保活（按照人为价格计算约为 46 分钟）。 让它消亡，重新填充，走开。
  • 留在付费范围内。 仅当您的暂停时间长于提供商的驱逐点（Anthropic ~5 分钟，OpenAI ~30 分钟，DeepSeek ~10 分钟，Gemini 从不）且短于其盈亏平衡点时才保持温暖。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 在他们的乐队内部节省了资金。 DeepSeek 和 Gemini 从不节省成本，只节省延迟。
  • 低于驱逐点，请勿打扰。 缓存本身仍然处于热状态，因此 ping 不会购买任何内容。 这是 30 秒惯例对每个提供商犯的错误。
  • 永远不要让死会话保持温暖。 pi 代理工具正是实现了这一点：仅在工具批处理运行时执行 ping 操作，默认关闭。

按照您的提供者自己的速度短暂保暖。 Ping 较少，但绝不会比缓存忘记的速度慢。
